# Keep the code search index across processes

## Intent

A caller that starts one `agentkit-tools` process per tool call must not pay
for a code search index on every call. The index and its symbol data are
kept on disk, outside the served directory, where the caller asks for them,
so a later process on the same directory reuses them and still answers as a
fresh build of the current tree would. An embedder that does not ask keeps
today's index, which lives and dies with its process.

## Goals

1. A second process on the same directory answers `code_search` and
   `find_symbol` from the index the first one built, without building again,
   and sees every file change made since.
2. The library offers the persistent directory as an option; with the option
   unset nothing changes.
3. `agentkit-tools` takes the directory from `--index-dir` or
   `AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR`, has no default location, and refuses one inside the
   served directory.
4. Two processes at once never read a half-written index, and only one of
   them builds.
5. On a generated tree of 10 000 source files, a `code_search` single call
   that finds a complete index and no changed file takes at most one fifth
   of the wall time of the call that built it, on the same machine.

## Non-goals

- The `agentkit-tools` command itself, its modes and its other flags: spec
  32 (`tool_server_command`).
- Removing the sandbox module: spec 31 (`sandbox_removal`).
- A default index location, in the library or the command (PRD 15 D6).
- Writing the changes a process revalidated back into the stored index. The
  stored index is replaced only by a build or by the rebuild the dirty
  threshold triggers today.
- Indexing from a git tree instead of a directory.
- Sharing an index between machines, or between two served directories.
- Changes to `code_search`'s or `find_symbol`'s arguments, results or
  descriptions.

## Background

`codesearch` (its own module on zoekt) builds the `code_search` index on the
first `code_search` call. `codesearch.New(ws, Options)` touches no disk;
`Options` has `MaxFiles`, `MaxBytes`, `MaxBuildTime` (60 s by default; a
build can run 1.25 times it) and `TempDir`. A build writes zoekt shards into
a run directory, `<TempDir>/agentkit-codesearch-<sha256 of the workspace
root>/<run id>`, and keeps in memory what the shards do not hold: the set of
indexed files, an `outline.File` per file for symbols, the size, modification
time and indexing time of each file, the build statistics, and whether the
build was partial and why. `Index.Close` deletes the run directory. A build
stopped by a bound leaves a partial index that the process does not retry;
results carry `partial` and `partial_reason`, and `Symbols` declines to
answer from a partial index.

Changes reach a live index through `Invalidate` (called by `write_file`,
`edit_file` and the shell tools), which marks paths dirty; a dirty mark makes
the next query revalidate: files whose size or modification time changed,
new files and deleted files are searched through a small overlay shard, and
more than five percent dirty triggers a full rebuild. A file edited within
the 2-second timestamp granule of its indexing is compared by content, with a
hash whose seed is chosen per process (`maphash.MakeSeed`), so it cannot be
compared across processes. Nothing marks a fresh process's index dirty: it
starts empty and builds.

`tools`' `find_symbol` asks `Index.Symbols` first, which answers only from an
index an earlier `code_search` of the same process built, is not partial and
not closed, and never starts a build; otherwise `find_symbol` builds its own
symbol table for the process, bounded at 2 seconds.

The tests live in `codesearch/index_test.go`
(`TestShardsLiveInARunDirectoryPerIndex`,
`TestCloseWaitsForTheFirstBuildAndRemovesItsRunDirectory`,
`TestBuildBoundsGiveAPartialIndexThatIsNotRetried`), `codesearch/dirty_test.go`
(`TestRevalidationFindsChangesMadeBehindTheToolsBack`,
`TestRevalidationInsideTheRacyWindowMarksOnlyRealEdits`),
`codesearch/symbols_test.go` (`TestSymbolsDeclinesWhenItCannotAnswerInFull`,
`TestFindSymbolGivesTheSameMatchesThroughTheIndex`) and
`codesearch/tool_test.go` (`TestTheFirstCodeSearchBuildsTheIndexOnce`), with
the fixtures of `codesearch/helpers_test.go`. The command of spec 32 lives in
`cmd/agentkit-tools`, with its tests beside it. The library reads no
`AGENTKIT_` variable (`docs/configuration.md`).

## Requirements

### A persistent index directory in the library

`codesearch.Options` gains `IndexDir`. Empty keeps today's behaviour: a run
directory under `TempDir` that `Close` deletes. Set, the index of a
workspace lives under `<IndexDir>/agentkit-codesearch-<sha256 of the
workspace root>/`, one such directory per served directory, so one index
directory holds the indexes of any number of them, kept apart. `Close` keeps
a stored index.

- `New` refuses an `IndexDir` that is the workspace root or lies inside it,
  after resolving symbolic links of the parts that exist, with an error that
  says it must be outside; it still touches no disk.
- A completed build is stored: the shards and everything the index keeps in
  memory beside them (the indexed files, the outlines, the size,
  modification time, indexing time and content hash of each file, the build
  statistics, the partial flag and reason), with a manifest naming the
  workspace root and the format version.
- A stored index becomes visible only when complete: it is written under a
  temporary name in the same directory and renamed into place, replacing the
  previous one.
- If the index directory cannot be created or written, the build is still
  used by the process from its run directory under `TempDir`, as today;
  `code_search` works, nothing is stored, and the result reports nothing
  unusual.

### Reuse and revalidation in a later process

- A process whose first `code_search` finds a complete stored index for its
  workspace root, in the current format, loads it instead of building, and
  revalidates before answering: files whose size or modification time
  changed since they were indexed, new files and deleted files are picked
  up. The answer is the same as from a fresh build over the current tree.
- A file indexed within the timestamp granule of its last modification is
  compared by content in the later process too: the stored content hash does
  not depend on the process that wrote it.
- A process that finds no index, an index whose manifest names another root,
  one written in another format version, or one it cannot read, builds a new
  one and replaces what was there. It reports nothing to the caller beyond
  the normal result.
- More than five percent of the files changed triggers the full rebuild it
  triggers today, and that rebuild is stored.

### Two processes and partial builds

- Two processes on the same workspace and index directory at once: one
  builds, holding a lock in the workspace's index directory; the other waits
  for the lock up to 1.25 times `MaxBuildTime` plus 5 seconds, then loads
  what the first stored. If the wait runs out, it builds for itself in its
  own run directory and stores nothing. Neither ever reads a half-written
  index. The lock is released when its holder exits, however it exits.
- A build stopped by its bounds stores a partial index, marked as such;
  results carry the partial marker as today. A later process that finds a
  partial stored index builds again, and replaces it.

### `find_symbol` from the stored index

`Index.Symbols` answers from a complete stored index in a process where no
`code_search` has run yet: it loads and revalidates the index, never builds
one, and returns the same matches as it would after a build. So a single
`find_symbol` call does not build a symbol table. It still declines a
partial stored index and a workspace with no stored index, as today.

### The command's index directory

- `agentkit-tools` takes `--index-dir <path>` on every subcommand, or the
  environment variable `AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR` when the flag is absent; the flag
  wins. An empty value means unset. There is no default location: without
  either, the index lives in a temporary directory removed when the process
  ends, as for a library embedder today.
- The command creates the directory when it is missing.
- An index directory that is the served directory or lies inside it exits 2
  with one line on stderr saying it must be outside, so an index is never
  checkpointed or committed with the work.
- If the index directory cannot be created or written, the command says so
  once on stderr, naming the directory, and serves `code_search` with a
  temporary index for that process.
- Target: on a generated tree of 10 000 source files, a `code_search`
  single call that finds a complete index and no changed file takes at most
  one fifth of the wall time of the call that built the index.

### Docs

`docs/codesearch.md` describes the stored index (layout, manifest, lock,
reuse, revalidation, partial builds); `docs/configuration.md` lists
`codesearch.Options.IndexDir` and `AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR`; `docs/cli.md`
documents `--index-dir` and the variable; `docs/guide.md` shows a relay that
names an index directory. `make doc` refreshes `docs/generated/`.

### End-to-end flows

1. **Relay from outside.** A relay writes a request file and runs
   `agentkit-tools call --dir <checkout> --index-dir <dir> --request <file>`
   for `code_search`, twice. The first process builds and stores the index;
   the second loads it, does not build, and returns the same files.
2. **A change between two processes.** A harness session with
   `--index-dir` searches, then edits a file with `edit_file` and closes. A
   later single call searches for the edit: it loads the stored index,
   revalidates and finds the edited file.
3. **Two processes at once.** Two single calls start at the same moment on
   a fresh index directory. One builds, the other waits and loads; both
   return the same result, and the index was built once.

## Design Decisions

1. **The index directory has no default location** (owner's decision, PRD
   15 D6). The caller that wants reuse names it; Parley's route always does.
2. **The option is `codesearch.Options.IndexDir`, and the library reads no
   environment variable** (decided from `docs/configuration.md`, which says
   the library reads no `AGENTKIT_` variable): `AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR` is the
   command's.
3. **The library refuses an `IndexDir` inside the workspace too** (decided
   here): otherwise the walk would index the shards themselves. The command
   checks first, to give its own message and exit 2.
4. **A store that fails falls back silently in the library; the command
   probes the directory first** (decided here): the library has no channel
   to a caller's stderr, so the command creates the directory and writes and
   removes a probe file before it starts, prints its one line on failure and
   passes no `IndexDir`.
5. **The waiting process's bound is 1.25 × `MaxBuildTime` + 5 s** (decided
   from `Options.MaxBuildTime`'s documented maximum build time); after it, the
   waiter builds for itself without storing, so a stuck builder cannot stall
   it forever. The lock is an advisory file lock, which the kernel releases
   when its holder exits.
6. **Revalidated changes are not written back** (decided here, also a
   non-goal): only a build or a threshold rebuild replaces the stored index,
   so a reader never races a partial update.
7. **A partial stored index is rebuilt, not served, by a later process**
   (PRD 15: "A later process tries the build again"). The process that built
   it keeps serving it, as today.
8. **The stored content hash is process-independent** (decided from
   `dirty.go`, whose per-process `maphash` seed cannot compare across
   processes): a hash function with a fixed definition, such as SHA-256.
9. **A manifest and a format version decide compatibility** (decided here):
   an index whose manifest names another root, another format version, or
   which does not parse is treated as absent.
10. **The wall-time target is a slow test** (decided here): it generates
    10 000 files and compares two wall times, so it is skipped under
    `-short` and runs in `make check-release`, the owner's run.
11. **Profile: full.** Reuse is verified across real processes of the
    command.
12. **Depends on spec 32**: the command's flag lands in the command it adds.

## Dependencies

- Spec 32 `tool_server_command` (active): the command that takes
  `--index-dir`.
- PRD 15 (`docs/prd/15-serve-the-tools-from-one-command-and-drop-the-sandbox.md`):
  the source; this package is its third scope.
- Archived spec 03 (`indexed_code_search`): the index this package persists,
  its bounds, revalidation and partial builds unchanged in contract.
- Parley (`github.com/agent-fox-dev/parley`): its route names the index
  directory.

## Verified External API

Read in this repository's sources:

- `codesearch.New(ws *workspace.Workspace, opts codesearch.Options) (tools.Index, error)`;
  `codesearch.Options{MaxFiles, MaxBytes, MaxBuildTime, TempDir}`;
  `(*codesearch.Index).Build`, `BuildCount`, `RevalCount`, `RunDir`,
  `IndexedFiles`, `Symbols`, `Invalidate`, `Close`.
- `tools.Index` (`Symbols(ctx, SymbolQuery) (SymbolAnswer, bool, error)`,
  `Tools`, `Invalidate`, `Close`).
- `github.com/sourcegraph/zoekt/search.NewDirectorySearcher(dir string)`, as
  `codesearch/overlay.go` calls it.
- `workspace.Workspace.Root() string`.

## Glossary

- **Index directory**: where the persistent `code_search` index and symbol
  data are kept, outside the served directory (`IndexDir`,
  `--index-dir`, `AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR`).
- **Stored index**: one workspace's complete or partial index in the index
  directory, with its manifest.
- **Served directory**: the directory given with `--dir`, opened as the
  workspace.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: A persistent index directory in the library

**Rationale:** A caller that runs one process per call must be able to keep the index where the next process finds it, without changing anything for an embedder that does not ask.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHERE Options.IndexDir is empty, THE codesearch SHALL keep the index in a run directory under TempDir that Close deletes, as before this package
   → after Close, the run directory and the per-workspace directory under TempDir are gone and nothing was written anywhere else
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go: TestCloseWaitsForTheFirstBuildAndRemovesItsRunDirectory and TestShardsLiveInARunDirectoryPerIndex keep passing unchanged with the zero IndexDir
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHERE Options.IndexDir is set and a build completes, THE codesearch SHALL store the index under <IndexDir>/agentkit-codesearch-<sha256 of the workspace root>/: the shards, the indexed files, the outlines, each file's size, modification time, indexing time and content hash, the build statistics and the partial flag and reason, with a manifest naming the workspace root and the format version, and keep it on Close
   → after a code_search and Close, the per-workspace directory holds the manifest and the shards; two workspaces sharing one IndexDir get two directories, each with its own root in its manifest
   Check: unit
   - setup: two temporary workspaces A and B and one temporary IndexDir, outside both
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go, a new test beside TestShardsLiveInARunDirectoryPerIndex: for ws in {A, B}: idx = indexFor(t, ws, {IndexDir: D}); find(t, idx, 'needle'); idx.Close(); dir = D/agentkit-codesearch-<sha256(ws.Root())>; assert dir holds a manifest naming ws.Root() and the format version, and at least one shard; assert the two directories differ
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF Options.IndexDir is the workspace root or lies inside it, after resolving the symbolic links of the parts that exist, THEN THE codesearch SHALL refuse to create the index, touching no disk
   → New returns a nil tools.Index and an error saying the index directory must be outside the workspace; nothing is created
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go, beside TestNewRefusesANilWorkspaceWithANilInterface, a table over IndexDir in {root, root/sub, root/missing/deeper, a symlink outside that points into root}: idx, err = New(ws, {IndexDir: d}); assert idx == nil (the interface itself); assert err mentions 'outside'; assert the tree under root is unchanged and d/missing was not created
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] THE codesearch SHALL for any build that stores an index, make it visible only when complete, by writing it under a temporary name in the per-workspace directory and renaming it into place over the previous one
   → while a build is between writing its shards and storing, the per-workspace directory holds no manifest for it and a loader finds no index; after the rename the manifest and shards are present and no temporary name remains
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hook that blocks a build after its shards are written and before the rename
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go: start a code_search on idx with IndexDir D; when the hook fires, assert the per-workspace directory has no complete index (the load function reports none) and only temporary names; release; after the call, assert the manifest exists and no temporary name is left
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] IF the index directory cannot be created or written, THEN THE codesearch SHALL use the build from a run directory under TempDir for the process, store nothing, and answer as usual
   → code_search is ok: true with the same files as without IndexDir and no field it would not otherwise carry; nothing is written under IndexDir
   Check: unit
   - setup: skipped as root and on Windows
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go, a table over IndexDir in {a path below a regular file, a directory with mode 0500}: idx = indexFor(t, ws, {IndexDir: d, TempDir: T}); r = find(t, idx, 'needle'); assert r.OK and paths(r) == the paths without IndexDir; assert r.Data has the same keys; assert idx.RunDir() is under T; assert nothing new under d
   ```

### REQ-2: Reuse and revalidation in a later process

**Rationale:** Reuse is only worth having if the answer is the one a fresh build of the current tree would give.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN the first code_search of an Index finds a complete stored index for its workspace root in the current format, THE codesearch SHALL load it instead of building, and revalidate the whole tree against it before answering
   → BuildCount() is 0 after the query; RevalCount() is at least 1; the result lists the same files as the process that built it
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/tool_test.go, beside TestTheFirstCodeSearchBuildsTheIndexOnce: a = indexFor(t, ws, {IndexDir: D}); ra = find(t, a, 'needle'); a.Close(); b = indexFor(t, ws, {IndexDir: D}); rb = find(t, b, 'needle'); assert b.BuildCount() == 0; assert b.RevalCount() >= 1; assert paths(rb) == paths(ra)
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] THE codesearch SHALL for any set of changes made to the tree between the process that stored the index and a later one (an edit that changes a file's size, one that changes only its modification time, a new file, a deleted file), answer in the later process as a fresh build over the current tree would
   → for each query, the later Index's result lists the same files, in the same order, as a new Index without IndexDir built over the same tree
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/dirty_test.go, beside TestRevalidationFindsChangesMadeBehindTheToolsBack, a table over the change kinds of the action (each written with os functions, not through the tools, after a.Close()): b = indexFor(t, ws, {IndexDir: D}); fresh = indexFor(t, ws, {}); for q in the queries that match the changed, new and deleted files: assert paths(find(t, b, q)) == paths(find(t, fresh, q)); assert b.BuildCount() == 0 unless the change set passes the rebuild threshold
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE codesearch SHALL compare by content, in a later process too, a file that was indexed within the timestamp granule of its last modification, using a stored content hash that does not depend on the process that wrote it
   → an edit that keeps a file's size and modification time, made within the granule after it was indexed, is found by the next process
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/dirty_test.go, beside TestRevalidationInsideTheRacyWindowMarksOnlyRealEdits: write f, index it with a (IndexDir D) at once, a.Close(); rewrite f with same-length content holding 'fresh_marker' and restore its modification time with os.Chtimes; b = indexFor(t, ws, {IndexDir: D}); assert 'f' in paths(find(t, b, 'fresh_marker')); and the stored hash of a file equals the hash function's value for its bytes in a separate call, independent of the process seed
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF the per-workspace directory holds no index, an index whose manifest names another root, one written in another format version, or one that cannot be read, THEN THE codesearch SHALL build a new index, store it in place of what was there, and answer as for a first build
   → BuildCount() is 1; the result is the normal result with no extra field; afterwards the manifest names this root and the current format version
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go, a table over the states {empty directory; manifest with another root; manifest with format version + 1; manifest that is not JSON; manifest present and a shard truncated to 0 bytes}: prepare D's per-workspace directory; idx = indexFor(t, ws, {IndexDir: D}); r = find(t, idx, 'needle'); assert r.OK and idx.BuildCount() == 1; assert r.Data's keys are those of any first build; assert the manifest now names ws.Root() and the current version
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] WHEN a process finds more than five percent of the indexed files changed against a stored index, THE codesearch SHALL run the full rebuild it runs today and store its result in place of the stored index
   → the rebuild happens once; afterwards the stored manifest is newer and a further process loads the rebuilt index without building
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/tool_test.go, extending TestMoreThanFivePercentDirtyRebuildsTheIndex to IndexDir D: a builds and closes; change more than 5% of the files; b = indexFor(... D); find(t, b, q); assert the rebuild ran once and the stored manifest changed; b.Close(); c = indexFor(... D); find(t, c, q); assert c.BuildCount() == 0
   ```

### REQ-3: Two processes at once and partial builds

**Rationale:** A relay may start two calls on one checkout at the same moment, and neither may read a half-written index or build twice.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN two Index values, in one process or in two, need the index of the same workspace in the same IndexDir at once and none is stored, THE codesearch SHALL let one build while holding an advisory file lock in the per-workspace directory, and let the other wait for the lock and then load what the first stored
   → both results list the same files; the builds of the two add up to 1
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go, beside TestCallsBehindTheFirstBuildShareIt: a, b = indexFor(... D) twice over the same ws; run find(t, a, q) and find(t, b, q) concurrently; assert paths equal; assert a.BuildCount() + b.BuildCount() == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] IF the lock is still held when the waiter has waited 1.25 times MaxBuildTime plus 5 seconds, THEN THE codesearch SHALL build for itself in its own run directory under TempDir and store nothing
   → the waiter's result is ok: true; its BuildCount() is 1; the stored index, and the lock holder, are untouched
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hook that holds the lock as another builder would, and a wait bound shortened through a test seam so the test does not wait the real bound
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go: hold the lock; idx = indexFor(... D); r = find(t, idx, q); assert r.OK and idx.BuildCount() == 1; assert idx.RunDir() is under TempDir; assert the per-workspace directory holds what it held before
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] THE codesearch SHALL release the lock when its holder exits, however it exits
   → after a process holding the lock is killed, a new Index takes the lock without waiting the bound
   Check: integration
   - setup: the test binary re-run as a helper process that takes the lock and sleeps; skipped on Windows
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go: start the helper (the test binary with a flag in its environment); wait until it holds the lock; kill it with SIGKILL; idx = indexFor(... D, MaxBuildTime: 60s); r = find(t, idx, q) under testutil.Within's bound, far below the 80 s wait; assert r.OK and idx.BuildCount() == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a build that stores its index is stopped by MaxFiles, MaxBytes or MaxBuildTime, THEN THE codesearch SHALL store the partial index marked as partial with its reason, serve it in the process that built it as today, and build again in a later process that finds it
   → the building process's results carry partial: true and partial_reason; a later Index finds the partial manifest, has BuildCount() == 1, and replaces the stored index
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/index_test.go, extending TestBuildBoundsGiveAPartialIndexThatIsNotRetried to IndexDir D with MaxFiles below the file count: r = find(t, a, q); assert r.Data.partial and r.Data.partial_reason == 'files'; assert the manifest is marked partial; a.Close(); b = indexFor(... D, no bound); find(t, b, q); assert b.BuildCount() == 1 and the manifest is no longer partial
   ```

### REQ-4: find_symbol from the stored index

**Rationale:** A single find_symbol call must not build a symbol table when a complete index of the tree is already stored.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN Symbols is called on an Index with a complete stored index and no code_search has run in its process, THE codesearch Index.Symbols SHALL load and revalidate the stored index without building, and answer from its outlines
   → ok is true; the matches equal those an Index that built the index returns; BuildCount() is 0; find_symbol through tools.For returns the same matches as without an index
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/symbols_test.go, extending TestFindSymbolGivesTheSameMatchesThroughTheIndex: a builds with IndexDir D and closes; edit one file to add func Fresh; b = indexFor(... D); ans, ok = b.Symbols(ctx, {Name: 'Fresh'}); assert ok and ans has Fresh in the edited file; assert b.BuildCount() == 0; and find_symbol through tools.For with b as Options.Index returns the matches tools.For without an index returns
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] IF Symbols is called on an Index whose stored index is partial or absent and no code_search has run in its process, THEN THE codesearch Index.Symbols SHALL decline without building, so find_symbol uses its own table as today
   → ok is false, the error is nil and BuildCount() is 0
   Check: unit
   ```
   in codesearch/symbols_test.go, extending TestSymbolsDeclinesWhenItCannotAnswerInFull with the cases {IndexDir D empty; D holding a partial stored index}: _, ok, err = idx.Symbols(ctx, q); assert !ok and err == nil and idx.BuildCount() == 0
   ```

### REQ-5: The command's index directory

**Rationale:** The relay names the index directory on the command line or in the environment of the process it starts, and must never get an index inside the work it checkpoints.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN a subcommand runs with --index-dir set to a non-empty path, or without it and with AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR set to a non-empty path, THE agentkit-tools SHALL create that directory when it is missing and give it to the index as its IndexDir, the flag winning over the variable
   → after a code_search call, the per-workspace directory with its manifest exists under the flag's directory when both are set, and under the variable's when only it is set; a missing directory has been created
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/agentkit-tools/index_test.go (new), a table over {flag F only (F missing); variable V only; both F and V; flag '' with V}: run(['call','--dir',D,'--request',R(code_search)] + flags, env); assert exit 0 and res.ok; assert a manifest exists under the expected directory (F, V, F, V) and nothing under the other
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] WHERE neither --index-dir nor AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR names a directory, THE agentkit-tools SHALL keep the index in a temporary directory that is removed when the process ends
   → after a code_search call exits 0, no agentkit-codesearch- directory is left under the process's TMPDIR
   Check: unit
   ```
   in cmd/agentkit-tools/index_test.go: run(['call','--dir',D,'--request',R(code_search)], env with TMPDIR=T and no AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR); assert exit 0 and res.ok; assert no entry of T starts with 'agentkit-codesearch-'
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A relay makes two single calls and the second reuses the index

1. **relay** writes a code_search request file and runs `agentkit-tools call --dir <checkout> --index-dir <dir> --request <file>`
2. **agentkit-tools** builds the index, stores it under <dir>, answers and exits 0
3. **relay** runs the same call again
4. **agentkit-tools** loads the stored index, revalidates, answers without building and exits 0

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the agentkit-tools binary, one process per call, the codesearch index on zoekt, the index directory on disk

**Setup:**

- a temporary checkout holding needle in a.go, and an empty index directory outside it
- the binary built from cmd/agentkit-tools; skipped where codesearch.New returns ErrUnsupported

**End state:**

- both results are ok: true and name the same files, a.go among them
- the index directory holds one per-workspace directory with a manifest naming the checkout
- the manifest's bytes and modification time, and the shards', are unchanged by the second call

**Pseudocode:**

```
in cmd/agentkit-tools/index_test.go: r1 = parse(run(call code_search with --index-dir X).stdout); m1 = stat and read X's manifest and shards; r2 = parse(run(the same).stdout); assert r1.ok and r2.ok and files(r1) == files(r2); assert X's manifest and shards equal m1
```

### PATH-2: A change made in a session is seen by a later single call

1. **harness** starts `agentkit-tools mcp --dir <checkout> --index-dir <dir>`, calls code_search, then edit_file to add fresh_marker to b.go, and closes the session
2. **agentkit-tools** builds and stores the index on the first search, and exits 0 when the session closes
3. **relay** runs `agentkit-tools call` for code_search of fresh_marker with the same --dir and --index-dir
4. **agentkit-tools** loads the stored index, revalidates, and returns b.go

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the agentkit-tools binary in mcp mode and in call mode, the MCP Go SDK client over CommandTransport, the codesearch index on zoekt, the index directory on disk

**Setup:**

- a temporary checkout of a few Go files and an empty index directory outside it
- skipped where codesearch.New returns ErrUnsupported

**End state:**

- the session's code_search found needle and its process exited 0
- the later single call's result is ok: true and names b.go for fresh_marker
- the stored manifest is the one the session's build wrote: the single call did not rebuild

**Pseudocode:**

```
in cmd/agentkit-tools/index_test.go: cs = client over CommandTransport(bin mcp --dir D --index-dir X); cs.CallTool(code_search 'needle'); cs.CallTool(edit_file add fresh_marker to b.go); cs.Close(); m = read X's manifest; res = parse(run(['call','--dir',D,'--index-dir',X,'--request',R(code_search 'fresh_marker')]).stdout); assert res.ok and 'b.go' in res.text; assert X's manifest == m
```

### PATH-3: Two single calls start at once on a fresh index directory

1. **relay** starts two `agentkit-tools call` processes for code_search at the same moment, with the same --dir and --index-dir
2. **agentkit-tools** in one process takes the lock, builds and stores the index; in the other waits for the lock and loads it
3. **relay** reads both results

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** two agentkit-tools processes, the advisory file lock, the codesearch index on zoekt, the index directory on disk

**Setup:**

- a temporary checkout and an empty index directory outside it; skipped on Windows and where codesearch.New returns ErrUnsupported

**End state:**

- both processes exit 0 with ok: true and the same files
- the per-workspace directory holds exactly one stored index with its manifest and no temporary name

**Pseudocode:**

```
in cmd/agentkit-tools/index_test.go: start p1 and p2 = run(call code_search --index-dir X) without waiting; wait both; assert both exit 0 and their results' files are equal; assert X's per-workspace directory lists one manifest and no temporary entry
```

### PATH-4: A maintainer checks the change and reads its docs

1. **maintainer** runs `make check` and `make doc` at the repository root
2. **Makefile** runs fmt, vet, lint and the short tests in every module MODULES lists, codesearch and cmd/agentkit-tools among them, and writes the generated docs
3. **maintainer** reads docs/codesearch.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/cli.md and docs/guide.md for the stored index, IndexDir, --index-dir and AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** the Makefile, the go toolchain, golangci-lint, git, the docs

**Setup:**

- a checkout of the branch; provider credentials scrubbed from the environment (env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY)

**End state:**

- `make check` exits 0
- `make doc` leaves `git status --porcelain` empty and docs/generated/codesearch documents Options.IndexDir
- docs/codesearch.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/cli.md and docs/guide.md each name what REQ-6.1 lists, and their Contents links resolve

**Pseudocode:**

```
a shell session, not a committed test: `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u OPENROUTER_API_KEY make check` exits 0; `make doc && git status --porcelain` is empty; grep docs/generated/codesearch/codesearch.txt for IndexDir; grep the four docs for IndexDir, AGENTKIT_INDEX_DIR and --index-dir
```

### 3. Build once when two processes need the index at once, and retry partial builds (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-3

**Steps:**

- 3.1 Before loading or building with IndexDir set, take an advisory lock on a lock file in the per-workspace directory (flock on the platforms codesearch builds for; windows/amd64 has the stub), and release it after the store
- 3.2 A process that finds the lock held waits for it, abandonably with its context, up to 1.25 times MaxBuildTime plus 5 seconds, then loads what the holder stored; past the bound it builds in its own run directory under TempDir and stores nothing; keep the bound behind a test seam
- 3.3 Store a build stopped by MaxFiles, MaxBytes or MaxBuildTime as partial, with its reason in the manifest; the building process keeps serving it with the partial marker as today, and a later process that finds a partial manifest builds again and replaces it
- 3.4 Write the behaviours of REQ-3 into codesearch/index_test.go beside TestCallsBehindTheFirstBuildShareIt and TestBuildBoundsGiveAPartialIndexThatIsNotRetried; the killed-holder test re-runs the test binary as a helper process
